title: The Toy Machine
blurb: Draw a map, freeze a brick, run it every frame.

chapters.title: Hello
chapters.text: Welcome to Grove. You draw a treasure map. Import freezes authoring Auth cards. Bake freezes a GraphData brick. A robot reads the brick every frame. Auth means authoring — not login.
chapters.deep: Grove is a three-layer package: Editor authoring, Authoring bake, and runtime execution. You author a Graph Toolkit asset that derives Grove Graph. Import produces a Grove Auth Graph. Baking produces a Blob Asset Reference of Graph Data on an I Graph Reference component. Runtime never reads the source map.

chapters.title: The main path
chapters.text: Follow the bright path. First you draw. Then the importer makes cards. Then the bake oven freezes everything into one brick called Graph Data. That brick is what play time uses.
chapters.deep: Pipeline: Grove Importer walks I Grove Nodes and subgraphs, sets Root when exactly one Input boundary resolves to an execution node, then Graph Authoring references the auth asset. Graph Baking Setup System reflects I Graph Baking types and creates Graph Baking System of T C. Auth Create builds the blob.

chapters.title: Helpers
chapters.text: Two helpers sit beside the path. Numbers on each box pick which door the robot opens. The backpack called Grove State remembers secrets between frames, like inputs and local variables.
chapters.deep: Each baked node is a header of Type int plus Node Id, then an inline payload. Execution Header Execute calls context Execution Generated, a source-generated switch. Live graph memory is the Grove State buffer, a dynamic untyped hash map keyed by Graph Id so multi-graph entities do not clobber each other.

chapters.title: Three rooms
chapters.text: There are three rooms. Draw time is Graph Toolkit. Bake time freezes the brick. Play time is your E C S system. Never mix the rooms up. The pretty map is not the brick.
chapters.deep: Bovine Labs Grove Editor owns Toolkit nodes and import. Grove Authoring owns auth assets and bakers. Grove runtime owns Graph Impl, Graph Execution, built-in nodes, and the source generator contract. Your I System owns one Graph Impl and builds a Graph Execution each update after Set Chunk.
